title.narrative: Joint Programs - Evaluation of Relevance and Impact on Resilience in Guatemala
Joint Programs - Utvärdering av relevans och inverkan på resiliens i Guatemala

description.narrative: En konsulttjänst kommer att upphandlas för utförande av en utvärdering av de tre gemensamma FN-programmen som finansieras genom den bilaterala strategin för utvecklingssamarbete med Guatemala 2016-2020. Utvärderingen kommer att fokusera på relevans och resultat av programmen och deras förmåga att bidra till resilienta system och samhällen på lokal nivå. Den kommer även att bidra till att bättre förstå vad som fungerar och vad som kan förbättras i de gemensamma programmen

The procured evaluation services will contribute to better understand what works and what can be improved in the Joint Programs working to strengthen the resilience of vulnerable rural populations in Guatemala. In order to ensure a better impact in result 8 of Sweden Development Cooperation Strategy with Guatemala. The evaluation will assess the impact and relevance of the contributions: 55200009, 55200010, 55200011 and 64000089.

The purpose or intended use of the evaluation is to provide Sida, through the Embassy of Sweden in Guatemala and its implementing partners in the country, with evidence and the opinion of a third party on what works to promote resiliencein beneficiaries and recommendations on what needs to be improved to ensure quality relevance and impact of interventions in the area of resilience and climate change adaptation under modality of Joint Programs. The scope of the evaluation is determine if Joint Program implementation and organizational scheme are relevant and effective to reach impact for strengthen resilience and climate change adaptation as stated in result 8 of development cooperation strategy. The programs included in the evaluation are: Joint Program Ixil (ongoing), Joint Program Cuilco (ongoing), Dry Corridor Program (ongoing), and Joint Program Coatan Suchiate (Closed). The implementing partners are: UNDP, FAO, PAHO/WHO and UNICEF.

Findings, recommendations and conclusions have been useful for learning, to identify best practices and to support next development programs. The evaluation foundd the programs to be relevant, effective and sustainable, with coherence with target group needs and to national develpment policies and strategies. The evaluation identified that the joint program model is relevant to tackle multidimensional poverty privations. As well, presented recommendations to facilitate the evolution of the model and ensure learning. The evaluation results have been incorporated in the design of new joint development programs in Guatemala.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
